Two-signal dirty check. Cell is dirty if: (1) fragment HTML != __source.value, OR (2) any history entry timestamp > __lastSyncedHistoryAt. Writes merged blobs, creates merge commit. On resolver failure throws MergeFailure after stashing backup branch at oursSha — nothing is lost.

export function buildPrompt(options: {
  sourceLanguage: string; targetLanguage: string; systemPrompt: string
  sourceText: string; examples: { source: string; target: string }[]
}): ChatMessage[] {
  const sys = options.systemPrompt
    .replace(/\{sourceLanguage\}/g, options.sourceLanguage)
    .replace(/\{targetLanguage\}/g, options.targetLanguage)

  let user = ""
  for (const ex of options.examples) user += `Source: ${ex.source}\nTranslation: ${ex.target}\n\n`
  user += `Source: ${options.sourceText}\nTranslation:`

  return [{ role: "system", content: sys }, { role: "user", content: user.trim() }]
summary: buildPrompt constructs the LLM chat messages from sourceLanguage, targetLanguage, systemPrompt, sourceText, and an array of examples. Examples are formatted as "Source: {source}\nTranslation: {target}" pairs in the user message.

authMiddleware at src/middleware/auth.ts:13-164 is the single JWT validation pipeline every authenticated route flows through. Pipeline: extractTokenFromHeader → JWTService.verifyToken (HS256 + SECRET_KEY via hono/jwt) → check exp → load user from D1 users table by sub claim → admin fallback (SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME / ADMIN_USERNAMES env) → Hetzner fallback (opaque token validated via HETZNER_API_URL, migration-phase). optionalAuthMiddleware + adminAuthMiddleware are sibling entry points. Any new sync-token code reuses this same middleware to validate the incoming Frontier JWT.

FileSync DO in sync-worker/src/index.ts — extends YServer from y-partyserver v2.1.4. static options = { hibernate: true }, callbackOptions debounceWait 2000ms debounceMaxWait 10000ms. onLoad reads projects/{projectId}/files/{fileId}/snapshot.bin + all tail/*.bin sorted by key then applies via Y.applyUpdate. onSave writes full Y.encodeStateAsUpdate to tail/{16-digit-ms-timestamp}.bin (padded for lexicographic sort). projectId is the spike stub "spike" until /sync-token wires in the real claim. Client connects via y-partyserver/provider with party: "file-sync" (class name kebab-cased). R2 binding name SNAPSHOTS → bucket codex-snapshots.

computeHealthMap(fileCells, llmHealthMultiplier=0.9, rules, rulePenalties={major:15,minor:5}) produces per-cell/file/project health. Per-cell rule: empty→skip; validationStatus full|self|others→100; none→average of healthMap[exId] for exIds in last history entry's examples, times llmHealthMultiplier (0 if no examples). Then subtracts rule-infraction penalties (clamped ≥0). File health = mean of non-empty cell healths; project health = mean across files. Key dependency: LLM cells get non-zero health only if their last history entry's `examples` array references OTHER cells that already have health in the map.

useSearchIndex IGNORES its first arg (_files: FileReference[]) and only indexes `currentCells` (the currently open file's cells) via buildFromProject([{fileId:'current', cells: currentCells}]). Effect re-runs on every currentCells identity change (cheap but frequent). Consequence: few-shot search for predictions only finds examples inside the active file, and only among cells whose `translated` is non-empty (see search-index.ts addPair guard). A fresh file with no translations yet produces zero search results → new LLM predictions get empty `examples` array → health-engine scores them 0.
